newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges private firms to set up accounts.
newsitem.headline: China urges private firms to set up accounts.

text.p: China's tax authorities have ordered private firms to set up standardised accounts from April 1 to ensure efficient tax collection, officials said on Monday.

The notice jointly issued by the State Council, or cabinet, and the State Administration of Taxation was aimed at regulating tax payment by private enterprises, an official of the State Administration of Taxation said.
Under the notice, private firms must set up nationwide standard accounts from April 1, then tax officials can collect taxes according to their accounts, she said but gave no further details.
Growing defaults in tax payments by enterprises have been hampering collection.
By the end of February, about 35.641 billion yuan of taxes remained unpaid by enterprises, an increase of 11.4 billion yuan compared with the same period of last year, state media said.
